title: Director, HW Engineering, AWS EC2
descriptionHtml:
Amazon EC2 Hardware Engineering designs and builds the servers that power Amazon Web Services. We take the silicon our partners create and design the boards, servers, and racks around it, then own the full lifecycle: new product introduction (NPI), design validation, launch, manufacturing ramp, and in-fleet sustaining engineering across compute, storage, networking, edge, and accelerator products.
We are looking for a world-class engineering leader (Director, Hardware Development) to own a server product line end to end. This is a hands-on hardware-engineering leadership role: your organization owns the hardware design, system integration, and system engineering for a product family, and is accountable for delivering it from design through volume manufacturing and into a large-scale global fleet that must run reliably for years.
This is a leadership role with exceptional surface area. The space is broad, and the depth is multilayered: you will lead multiple teams through their managers, set multi-year technical and product strategy for your product line, operate deep in the engineering when it matters, and work externally with ODMs and vendors at a detailed technical level to drive roadmaps and secure supply. You will partner with the component and firmware teams your products depend on, and with Principal and Distinguished Engineers and senior leaders across AWS. The problems are hard, the scale is among the largest in the world, and the work is visible to the most senior leaders at AWS.


Key job responsibilities
As the Director, Hardware Development, you will:
• Own a server product family end to end: hardware design, system integration, and system engineering, from NPI (New Product Introduction)and design validation through launch, manufacturing ramp, and in-fleet sustaining.
• Own hardware quality and velocity for your product line, and be accountable for manufacturing yield and throughput targets and for resolving manufacturing-engineering defects.
• Lead multiple engineering teams through their managers; hire, grow, and develop managers and engineers, and scale the organization to meet an aggressive roadmap.
• Set the multi-year technical and product strategy for your product line and make long-term engineering decisions that balance innovation with reliability at scale.
• Manage strategic relationships with ODM design and manufacturing partners (domestic and overseas)
• Own fleet-reliability outcomes for your products (annualized failure rate, unsellable reduction, proactive defect remediation).
• Partner across hardware, firmware, software, operations, and supply chain, and drive external roadmaps with partner teams.


A day in the life
You will work on problems that do not have textbook answers and where the questions themselves may not even be known. How do you take a new accelerator, compute, or storage server from a concept through qualification and ramp at an ODM, and into a global fleet that fails less than a fraction of a percent of the time over a ten-year life? How do you re-architect a design to hit manufacturing throughput targets for hundreds of thousands of units with minimal waste? How do you qualify a second source for a critical component to de-risk supply without slipping a launch? You will take hardware from a whiteboard sketch through design, manufacturing, and deployment at a scale almost nowhere else can offer.

About the team
EC2 Hardware Engineering is organized along a vertical (product) and horizontal (component and firmware) axis. Vertical teams own whole server products end to end; the horizontal teams own the cross-cutting components and firmware every product depends on. This role leads one of the vertical product organizations. We invest in bringing new members up to speed, and we think about each engineer's growth when we assign work.

Basic qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or commensurate experience
• 10+ years of hardware development experience
• 8+ years of engineering management experience
• Experience delivering complex integrated hardware systems (servers, racks, or comparable electro-mechanical/compute systems) from design through volume manufacturing
• Experience owning the full product lifecycle: NPI, design validation, launch, manufacturing ramp, and in-field sustaining
• Experience partnering with product/program management and operating hardware at scale

Preferred qualifications

• Experience designing and delivering datacenter server and/or rack systems at hyperscale
• Deep experience in one or more of: board/system design, PCIe and high-speed signal integrity, power delivery and thermal, accelerator (GPU) systems, x86/ARM compute, or storage (HDD/SSD) systems
• Design-for-manufacturing expertise; experience managing ODM partners (domestic and overseas) and component multi-sourcing/qualification
• Experience operating a hardware fleet at scale: telemetry, real-time health, annualized-failure-rate reduction, and sustaining engineering
• Experience with taking new greenfield technology initiatives or cutting-edge development to large scale production of integrated systems
• Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a relevant engineering discipline

title: Construction Safety Manager (CSM), DCPD Health and Safety
descriptionHtml:
Do you enjoy taking an idea and turning it into something? Do you ever find yourself marveling at buildings, infrastructure, or landmarks and ask "what does it take to build something like that?" The Construction Safety Manager role is for an experienced Health and Safety (H&S) Specialist, H&S Engineer, or H&S Manager who will support AWS Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD) programs. Internally, you will partner with DCPD teams such as Real Estate, Due Diligence, Permitting, Energy, Water, Pre-Construction, Construction, Commissioning, Security and Procurement Teams to achieve health and safety goals and improve our safety culture. Externally, you will engage with General Contractors and AWS Suppliers to confirm/clarify the business expectations for H&S, and look for ways to continually improve H&S of our contracted services. You will work under the direction of the AMER Regional Health & Safety Manager.

Key job responsibilities
This is a field based role, required to report to work at field construction projects in Texas five days per week. Occasional travel to other domestic locations may be required.

You will influence program development, framework, and strategy while deploying programs in the field. This role encompasses implementing health and safety programs across leadership, planning, support, operational controls, continuous improvement, and performance management. You will ensure construction activities meet jurisdictional requirements and AWS Safety Management Program (SMP) standards through systematic compliance and assurance activities.

Examples:
• Review due diligence risk assessments with real estate, pre-construction, construction operations on H&S aspects of the AWS H&S management program to ensure adequate implementation.
• Coordinates with DCPD managers to prioritize H&S in planning and execution in all phases of DCPD projects.
• Ensures & Monitors General Contractors and AWS deployment vendors compliance to onboarding requirements in Avetta.
• Performs campus H&S kickoff sessions, and performs reviews of General Contractor and AWS deployment vendor’s Construction Safety Management Plans
• Documents data and anecdotes in standard reporting tools (Weekly Business Reviews, Monthly Project Reviews) for DCPD and H&S leadership teams
• Manages 3rd party/internal H&S resources on DCPD projects (weekly business reviews, monthly project reviews)
• Identifies improvement opportunities at project(s), and partners with Data Center Health and Safety (DCHS) Operational Team on regional issues that impact construction/operations handover phases.
• Audits projects to the mental model ‘do you have a process, and are you following it?’ Then analyzes data (leading and lagging indicators) for trends, risks/opportunities and reports out at project/regional levels and within governance programs
• Conduct regular site visits with H&S Consultants, construction managers and Data Center Health and Safety Operational teams
• Hosts project and regional specific contractor and internal team H&S kickoff sessions and annual performance review sessions.

A day in the life
This is a field based role, required to report to work at field construction projects in Texas, five days per week. Occasional travel to other domestic locations may be required. This is a unique role that for the right candidate has the potential to take ownership over the entire lifecycle of a Data Center. Starting as a Construction Safety Manager with DCPD on Construction Projects supporting Construction Managers and then transferring safety teams after construction to DCHS as a Regional Safety Manager for the very same buildings in support of Operational Leaders throughout the live space.

You will be integrated with a global network of H&S professionals including Program Managers, other Construction Safety Managers, and Construction Managers. Later in the lifecycle, there is the potential to partner with Operational leaders such as Cluster and Facility Managers, Security Teams, Environmental Partners, as well as other Health & Safety Managers.

You will use data and anecdotes to tactically drive internal customers to manage H&S risks, which includes being an escalation path for issue resolution and managing site-based H&S team members and/or consultants. You will apply your knowledge of the jurisdictional requirements, regional best practices, cultural norms, and location specific characteristics to improve DCPD activities in H&S by jumping in and showing the business “this is what the data is telling us, and this is what actions we should take” and develop DCPD competencies to enable them ownership of your solutions.

You must be an effective communicator, sending clear, concise and consistent messages verbally, in written form, and/or public speaking forums. You will play a key role in deploying mechanisms that manage H&S, while developing competencies and ownership of H&S in the business. You must have diplomacy, patience and tact to earn trust in relationships to effectively advise, instruct and challenge DCPD teams on H&S.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Enterprise Productivity - Communicate & Connect
descriptionHtml:
Enterprise Productivity (EP) Communicate & Connect is looking for an experienced Sr. Technical Program Manager (TPM) to be the program-management backbone of our newly combined pillar. The pillar owns how more than a million Amazon employees message, meet, call, and email, across Slack, Zoom, telephony, fax, and email. You will report directly to Suresh Selvaraj, the pillar’s single-threaded leader, and you will have two connected mandates.
First, you will partner closely with EP’s Principal Engineer for AI-native software development. Together you will turn a cross-cutting technical vision into a governed, measurable delivery program across 50+ services. Second, you will be the umbrella TPM for the whole org. You will own the single mechanism we use to track, report, and drive business deliverables, including our business reviews and long-term operational planning.

A successful candidate will also demonstrate:
• Comfort working with org-wide scope and high ambiguity, across first-party services and third-party SaaS platforms
• Ability to think strategically about a multi-year transformation while executing methodically week to week
• Enough technical depth to engage credibly with Principal Engineers on architecture, dependencies, and adoption
• Data fluency, using metrics and hard data to back up status, risks, and recommendations
• Clear, concise writing for Directors and VPs in Amazon narrative format
• An owner’s mentality and willingness to dive deep and do whatever is needed to deliver


Key job responsibilities
In this role:
- You partner with EP’s Principal Engineer to program-manage the AI-native SDLC transformation, including spec-driven development, AI-assisted code generation, automated testing, and intelligent CI/CD. You track adoption across Dublin teams and other locations.
- You coordinate delivery across the Principal Engineer’s principal-level workstreams: AI agent governance, email security modernisation, vendor API reliability and observability, and AI-native SDLC. You keep cross-team dependencies, decisions, and risks visible and on track.
- You own the business operating cadence for the entire Communicate & Connect org. You run business reviews end to end, including the narrative, the metrics, and putting the documents together.
- You build and maintain one deliverables tracker across every service. It maps commitments to goals, status, and risk, and you use it to hold teams accountable to dates.
- You combine team-level plans into the pillar’s operation plans and goal submissions, so EP leadership sees one coherent story.
- You lead cross-service programs spanning email, Slack, Zoom, and telephony. You influence priorities without direct authority and make data-backed cases for sequencing and resourcing.
- You spot delivery and operational risks early and bring them to leadership with mitigation plans before they become blockers.
- You are a simplifier. You add, refine, and retire mechanisms so teams spend less time on process and more on delivery.
- You take part in hiring and mentoring other TPMs and engineers on program management best practices.

A day in the life
In a typical week you might sync with the Principal Engineer on AI-native adoption progress and blockers, run a cross-service dependency review, pull metrics from service owners to update the deliverables tracker, and draft the pillar’s MBR narrative for EP leadership. You will move between deep technical conversations and executive business reviews, often on the same day.

About the team
Communicate & Connect is part of Enterprise Productivity, which owns crucial productivity services that power how more than a million Amazon employees create, communicate, collaborate, and operate. Our pillar puts messaging, meetings, voice, and email under one owner so customers never feel the seams between services.

We are working toward the EP vision, “Amazonians make the decisions. Our tools do the rest.” To get there, we are unifying the operational layer and applying one autonomous-operations playbook across email, Slack, Zoom, and voice. Our Dublin hub is EP’s largest engineering site outside the US and is central to this transformation. We value diverse perspectives and an inclusive culture grounded in Amazon’s Leadership Principles.

title: Senior Industrial Designer, Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) Design
descriptionHtml:
The Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) Design team is seeking an experienced Sr. Industrial Designer to join our Design Engineering team. Our team leads building design for large-scale industrial grocery facilities, including fulfillment and distribution centers, middle mile facilities, and other industrial grocery buildings across Amazon Grocery's network. We support ground-up, greenfield developments as well as the retrofit of existing facilities.

This individual will own composite drawing packages, construction documents, and permitting processes for large-scale industrial grocery facilities. The role spans the full spectrum of industrial development project types, including ground-up greenfield development, building shell design and delivery, and tenant improvement (TI) work within existing industrial facilities. The role requires deep industrial design expertise, technical precision, the ability to manage complex, multi-phase projects with ambiguous parameters, and the judgment to drive design decisions that balance operational efficiency, scalability, and cost effectiveness.

A successful candidate will thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment, collaborating with internal and external teams to generate high-quality, cost-effective design solutions. They will work across multiple projects with varied timelines while influencing, negotiating, and communicating effectively with internal stakeholders, contractors, engineers, and vendors.


Key job responsibilities
• Own end-to-end design support for large-scale industrial grocery facilities across the full project type spectrum: ground-up greenfield development, building shell design, and tenant improvement (TI) work within existing industrial facilities
• Work with vendors to develop, manage, and maintain composite drawing packages and construction document sets for large-scale industrial grocery facilities
• Lead shell design coordination, including site civil interface, structural systems, building envelope, and core-and-shell documentation for large-scale industrial facilities
• Manage tenant improvement design and documentation, adapting existing industrial shells to accommodate grocery fulfillment operations, automation systems, and food safety requirements
• Lead permitting processes across multiple jurisdictions, coordinating with local authorities, landlords, and regulatory bodies to ensure timely approvals for ground-up, shell, and TI scopes
• Partner with Real Estate, Pre-Construction, Construction, Program Management, and Operations Engineering teams throughout all project phases to align design with business requirements, schedule, and budget
• Collaborate with external architects and engineers to develop, coordinate, and finalize construction document and permitting packages
• Partner with internal and external engineering, operations, and construction teams to streamline site layouts, workstation configurations, and material flow for maximum efficiency and value
• Create scalable design solutions and execute them with clear communication and documentation, ensuring designs can be replicated and adapted across the network
• Maintain and enforce drawing standards across multiple business lines, and establish new standards for emerging building types and confidential strategic programs
• Support value engineering efforts on existing network sites, identifying opportunities to improve throughput, safety, and cost efficiency
• Drive programmatic rollouts for key design initiatives across the distribution center network
• Manage consultant and vendor relationships throughout all phases of design and construction administration
• Identify and mitigate design risks proactively, escalating to leadership when appropriate
• Communicate complex design concepts effectively to business partners at all levels, including senior leadership

A day in the life
If you thrive in an ever-changing, high-ambiguity environment, then we want to talk to you. This position works closely with cross-functional teams, external consultants, engineers, and vendors throughout the full development lifecycle of large-scale industrial facilities. You will serve as the primary design point of contact on complex projects while maintaining the confidence and judgment to know when to escalate. This candidate must have a professional and positive demeanor and be able to communicate effectively with business partners at every level, including leadership.

About the team
The Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) Design team is a fast-growing part of the larger Worldwide Grocery organization, responsible for all Grocery retail and industrial buildings. We work on a portfolio of strategic, high-impact projects across retail locations, greenfield developments, and retrofit of existing stores and facilities. We are an ambitious, innovative, and customer-obsessed team where everyone is entrepreneurial, wears many hats, and moves quickly. Our goal is to design and deliver world-class buildings that get the highest quality food to our customers as fast as possible.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering (any domain), Operations, Business Administration, or a related field
- Knowledge of AutoCAD 3D
- 5+ years of reading and understanding schematics and building drawings experience

Preferred qualifications

descriptionHtml:
When you attract people who have the DNA of pioneers and the DNA of explorers, you build a company of like-minded people who want to invent. And that’s what they think about when they get up in the morning: how are we going to work backwards from customers and build a great service or a great product” – Jeff Bezos
Amazon.com’s success is built on a foundation of customer obsession. Have you ever thought about what it takes to successfully deliver millions of packages to Amazon customers seamlessly every day like a clock work? In order to make that happen, behind those millions of packages, billions of decision gets made by machines and humans. What is the accuracy of customer provided address? Do we know exact location of the address on Map? Is there a safe place? Can we make unattended delivery? Would signature be required? If the address is commercial property? Do we know open business hours of the address? What if customer is not home? Is there an alternate delivery address? Does customer have any special preference? What are other addresses that also have packages to be delivered on the same day? Are we optimizing delivery associate’s route? Does delivery associate know locality well enough? Is there an access code to get inside building? And the list simply goes on. At the core of all of it lies quality of underlying data that can help make those decisions in time. title: Sr. Supplier Quality Engineer, Infrastructure Reliability & Quality
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services Infrastructure Reliability & Quality (IRQ) engineering team provides engineering support for our data center infrastructure mechanical and electrical equipment (Air Handling Unit, Switchgear, Breaker, Panel Board, UPS, Transformers, Generators, ATS etc.) as well as infrastructure security equipment (Cameras, Access Control, etc.) throughout their lifecycle. A critical piece of this support is ensuring the highest level of initial quality and ongoing support from our suppliers.

As a Senior Quality Engineer, you will ensure the highest standards of quality for AWS infrastructure equipment from supplier selection through field deployment. You will evaluate supplier capabilities through technical assessments and on-site evaluations, investigate quality issues using analytical approaches including failure mode analysis and apply engineering judgment to assess quality risks across design, manufacturing, and deployment stages. You will use critical thinking to drive field root cause analysis, identifying underlying failure mechanisms and developing effective corrective actions. Working closely with AWS Engineering teams, Procurement teams, Commissioning teams, and suppliers, you will develop data-driven insights from supplier performance metrics and field observations to drive improvements that enhance equipment quality. You will partner with engineering teams to define equipment specifications and acceptance criteria, work with suppliers to implement improvements through technical guidance and capability building, and collaborate with commissioning and operations teams to translate field performance findings into actionable quality improvements. You will also build and maintain quality roadmaps that align with AWS infrastructure goals, analyze trends across multiple equipment categories and suppliers to identify systemic quality challenges, and manage multiple concurrent quality initiatives across different regions and equipment types.

Keys to success in this role include sound judgment and excellent written/verbal communication skills.

Travel required, both international and domestic, approximately 30-50%

Key job responsibilities
In this role you will:
- Develop, implement and maintain the supplier quality roadmap across engineering and procurement teams.
- Conduct technical investigations of equipment failures to understand root causes and prevent recurrence
- Provide technical expertise on quality evaluation methods, testing approaches, and failure analysis techniques
- Drive supplier and product qualification and assessment processes in support of procurement teams. This includes developing technical approaches for evaluating new equipment and suppliers entering the AWS ecosystem
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives that address both immediate quality issues and long-term performance optimization
- Develop and implement Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to monitor supplier quality performance and drive accountability
- Work on concurrent projects, sometimes in multiple geographical regions.

A day in the life
Your day will be a dynamic blend of technical investigation, strategic problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration. You'll dive deep into equipment performance data, conduct detailed failure analyses, and develop innovative solutions that prevent future technical challenges. From remote meetings with global supplier teams to on-site technical assessments, you'll be at the forefront of maintaining AWS's infrastructure excellence.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Reliability & Quality (IRQ) engineering team provides engineering support for our data center infrastructure equipment (Air Handling Unit, Switchgear, Breaker, Panel Board, UPS, Transformers, Generators, ATS, Cameras, Access Control etc.) throughout their lifecycle. Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) team is part of the IRQ team and works on implementing proactive controls to reduce the incoming supplier quality issues.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field
- Experience in root cause analysis and troubleshooting or problem solving
- Experience working with equipment suppliers, laboratories and manufacturing plants
- Experience in gathering test requirements to create detailed test plans and defining quality metrics to measure product quality

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or above in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Experience in data center engineering or operations
- Experience in manufacturing, process, or industrial engineering
- Experience with process improvement, Kaizan, and Six Sigma, or experience in creating process improvements with automation and analysis
- Experience with data analysis tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, SQL, Tableau, etc.
- 6+ years of supply chain, forecasting, manufacturing, sourcing/procurement, or vendor management experience

title: Strategic Supply Chain Manager

Our team works across 14 countries spanning vastly different industries, stages of cloud maturity, and competitive landscapes. We partner closely with field sales, solutions architecture, and specialist teams to activate customers and ensure every engagement moves the needle. We are builders at heart — constantly evolving our content, mechanisms, and delivery models to stay ahead of the pace of change in AI and technology innovation. We're looking for a customer-obsessed Innovation Program Lead to drive customer impact through our innovation experiences — using Amazon culture and technology to help enterprise customers discover, invent, and build their way to production. This role is about delivering tangible business outcomes, helping customers realize value from their technology and AI investments by combining the best of how Amazon innovates with the power of AWS technology. You'll facilitate executive engagements, activate customers in partnership with field sales teams, build scalable mechanisms across our top customers, and lead the development of next-generation content. The nature of innovation is ever-changing, and this role requires someone who is deeply adaptable and energized by that pace of change.

Key job responsibilities
1. Customer Impact through Business, Technology & Culture Transformation
● Lead and facilitate executive-level innovation sessions that bring Amazon's culture of innovation — Working Backwards, customer obsession, bias for action — to life for customers. Create an environment where senior leaders engage deeply with new possibilities and leave with clear business outcomes in mind.
● Apply first-principles thinking to understand customers' most pressing challenges and translate those into actionable AI-driven solution pathways. Help customers adopt Amazon's innovation methods alongside AWS technology to drive real business results.
● Own the customer journey beyond the engagement — work closely with field sales teams to activate customers, drive solution adoption, and accelerate the path from idea to measurable business outcomes in production.
2. Mechanisms & Operational Excellence
● Design and implement scalable engagement frameworks. Leverage AI to streamline processes — from session preparation to insight capture — ensuring every customer interaction generates reusable learnings.
● Build the ability to scale innovation experiences across our top customers in the region, ensuring consistent quality and impact at volume while delivering business outcomes.
● Build strong operating interlocks with field sales teams, solutions architects, and partner organizations. Establish a clear operating model that makes it frictionless for account teams to activate customers into innovation experiences.
● Codify what works. Develop playbooks, templates, and tooling that enable other markets to replicate successful engagement patterns as the model expands across the region.
3. Content Leadership
● Build next-generation content modules focused on generative AI, agentic systems, and applied AI — grounded in Amazon's culture of innovation and maintained as a portfolio that is modular, industry-adaptable, and technically current.
● Elevate the delivery experience — integrate AI to personalize content in real-time, generate dynamic demonstrations, and create immersive customer experiences that bring Amazon culture and technology together in a way that sets us apart in the region.
● The nature of innovation is ever-changing. Maintain a forward-looking content roadmap, monitor industry signals, competitive moves, and customer patterns — and adapt quickly to ensure our offerings remain relevant as technology evolves.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of Go-To-Market, Business Development, Sales, or Consulting experience
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences
- Strong first-principles problem-solving ability — comfortable deconstructing ambiguous customer challenges into clear action plans that deliver business outcomes
- Strong ability to apply AI/ML capabilities to solve business problems and drive transformation outcomes, engaging both technical and business audiences on generative AI, agentic systems, and applied AI

descriptionHtml:
Deine Chance: Technik, die bewegt
Bei uns hältst du die Systeme am Laufen, die Produkte vom Klick bis zur Haustür bringen. Du analysierst Störungen, wartest komplexe Anlagen und arbeitest mit Mechanik, Elektrotechnik, Pneumatik und Steuerungssoftware, mit echtem Einfluss vom ersten Tag an.
Hier ist deine Arbeit nicht abstrakt. Sie ist sichtbar, unmittelbar und bedeutsam. Und dein Weg? Den gestaltest du selbst, mit endlosen Möglichkeiten, dich weiterzuentwickeln.

Du tüftelst gerne, packst mit an und willst früh Verantwortung übernehmen? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig.

Key job responsibilities
• Installation, Überwachung, Wartung und Instandhaltung mechanischer und elektrischer Anlagen.
• Analyse und Behebung von Störungen an automatisierten Systemen.
• Arbeiten in den Bereichen Metallbearbeitung, Elektrotechnik, Hydraulik, Pneumatik und Steuerungstechnik.

Du arbeitest von Anfang an Seite an Seite mit erfahrenen Techniker:innen, die dich fördern und fordern. Du übernimmst schrittweise mehr Verantwortung, probierst Dinge aus und lernst Fähigkeiten, von denen du vorher nicht wusstest, dass es sie gibt.

- Du hast mindestens einen Hauptschulabschluss zum Beginn der Ausbildung
- Fortgeschrittene Deutschkenntisse in Wort und Schrift (B2-Niveau)
- Gute Schulnoten in Mathematik und Physik (abhängig von der Schulform)

Preferred qualifications

- Grundkenntnisse in Englisch (A2-Niveau)
- Du bringst bereits erste Vorerfahrungen im handwerklichen Bereich mit

title: Data Center Engineering Operations - 2027 Internship , DCEO
descriptionHtml:
Want to be part of the team that keeps the world's largest cloud running? As an Engineering Operations Technician Intern at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will get hands-on experience with the critical infrastructure behind Amazon's global data centers — and your work will directly impact millions of customers worldwide.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Engineering Operations Technician position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

- Students in the last year of their Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.

It is a requirement to be graduated by the end of the internship.

Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying.

About the Role

As an intern, you will provide technical support within Amazon's owned and operated data centers. Your work will ensure that the data center's mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems operate at 100% availability while maintaining first-class customer service to the teams and groups on site.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do

The Engineering Operations team is Amazon's front-line responders for hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. You will work with equipment that supports mission-critical servers and must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. This equipment includes, but is not limited to:

- Stand-by diesel generators and switchgear

- Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPSs) and Power Distribution Units (PDUs)

- Air Handling Units (AHUs), chillers, and cooling towers

- Chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, and Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)

- Building automation systems

Your day-to-day duties include:

- Maintaining mechanical and electrical equipment

- Assisting with root cause analysis of equipment failures

- Troubleshooting facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

- Taking daily operational readings of all mechanical and electrical equipment

- Using internal Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) to manage building workflows

- Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 3 consecutive months, starting in summer 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Sunday through Thursday.

Please note that full-time Engineering Operations Technician roles operate on a rotating shift pattern, which may include days, nights, weekends, and public holidays. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will troubleshoot and maintain the systems that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale.

Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. From cloud computing to artificial intelligence, the systems you maintain power it all.

Action. You will move fast, experiment, and learn by doing. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.

Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.

Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Beyond that, you will find continuous learning opportunities and the chance to work on different projects. Your journey here is yours to shape.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.

You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

Basic qualifications

- In pursuit of a Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Mechanical Engineering or Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, graduating in 2027 - before the end of the internship.
- Professional English proficiency, both written and verbal
- Ability to work well with others in a team environment, with strong time management skills

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in program or project management
- Knowledge of mechanical systems (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning systems, controls)

title: Electric Vehicle Charger Specialist ,  Amazon Maintenance Operation Centre (AMOC)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Operations sits at the heart of the Amazon customer experience. We look after everything from the moment a customer clicks buy, to the moment their item is delivered – from desktop to doorstep.

Working in Amazon Operations is for people who like to be active and give their all. We work in a busy, dynamic environment and are part of a bigger team delivering on the expectations of millions of customers every single day. We are open, inclusive and welcome individuality and diversity. The culture in our operation is built on the way teams’ bond and the work ethic that enables our business run like clockwork. Our teams take pride in a job well done, looking out for one another, ensuring the highest safety standards and playing their part in delivering the quality service Amazon is known for around the world.
Amazon is committed to building a sustainable future for our customers, local communities, and the planet. Under The Climate Pledge we committed to be net-zero carbon across our business by 2040, 10 years ahead of the Paris Agreement. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people that are dedicated to making a meaningful impact on the sustainability of our products and supply chain.

Join us in the Amazon Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team. We maintain and optimize technologies in the Global Amazon Warehouse & Delivery Network.

Purpose of job

Amazon is a global leader in sustainable transportation solutions, dedicated to advancing the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and reducing our carbon footprint. Our state-of-the-art EV charging infrastructure continues to grow and span the globe, providing reliable and accessible charging solutions to drivers around Amazon’s transportation network. As an Electric Vehicle Charger Escalation Specialist, you will play a critical role in maintaining the functionality and reliability of our global network of Electric Vehicle (EV) chargers. You will be part of a 24/7 team responsible for remote coordination and escalation of maintenance and technical issues to ensure minimal downtime and optimal performance of our charging network.


Key job responsibilities
• Continuously monitor the performance of EV charging stations worldwide, identifying any technical issues or anomalies.
• Respond and process incoming alarms, trouble tickets, purchase orders, invoices following SOPs and processes.
• Serve as a point of contact for customers in the field when technical problems arise. Escalate issues to the appropriate vendors or teams for resolution.
• Maintain detailed records of technical issues, escalations, and resolutions. Use reports and dashboards to track the performance and reliability of the charging network.
• Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including RME field, operations, sustainability and external stakeholders, to ensure efficient issue resolution.
• Develop and improve training materials and resources to improve troubleshooting skills, reducing the need for escalations.
• Recommend process improvements and enhancements to the charging infrastructure based on insights gathered from issue analysis.

A day in the life
Your job is simple to describe and never boring to do: keep the EV chargers up and running.

You'll start each morning with the most urgent cases — the chargers that are down. For each one, you'll play detective: fix it remotely in minutes, or send someone to the site? When the cause isn't obvious, you'll dig into the charger's history to find the root problem, and know when to escalate.

Much of your day is making things happen through others — coordinating technicians and vendors, joining alignment meetings, and handling the paperwork: purchase requests, technical reports, quotes, and invoices.

About the team
You'll join a team that brings together two kinds of expertise. On one side are escalation specialists who come from a range of different backgrounds, united by solid experience in customer service and support — they know how to stay calm under pressure, keep people informed, and drive an issue through to resolution. On the other side are senior EV charger specialists, the technical experts who know these chargers inside and out and can get to the bottom of even the trickiest problems.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, Word, Outlook, etc.)
- Experience working independently and collaborating effectively in a remote team environment
- Experience in a 24/7 environment
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English at C1 level or above
- Experience in technical support, escalation management, or a similar role.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
- Experience in Electric vehicle charger industry or related industries
- Proficient in other languages

descriptionHtml:
Summary

The Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team at Amazon is fundamental to our operations – they're the ones keeping vital machinery running at all times. As an RME Technician, you'll maintain a wide range of equipment and workspaces while upholding Health and Safety best practices. You'll help to keep your colleagues safe and prevent machine downtime. Our RME Technicians boost the availability and quality of our equipment and work to enhance the operational environment too.

Shift Pattern: This role includes working in non-traditional shift pattern, which may include nights and weekends






Key job responsibilities
- Proactive and preventative maintenance tasks on a wide range of site equipment
- Carry out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
- Use the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
- Uphold all health and safety policies and practices
- Support the development and progression of on-site apprentices
- Work on continuous improvement projects and roll out best practices across a range of EU sites


A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You'll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites' equipment to make sure it's working safely. As an RME Technician, you'll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You'll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you'll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You'll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we're known for.

As a Cluster Technician, you'll be assigned a nodal home site that serves as your primary base. However, the role includes an element of travel within your designated cluster of sites. This means you'll move between locations as needed to provide maintenance support, respond to breakdowns, and carry out planned preventative work across multiple facilities. This travel element ensures our sites receive consistent, high-quality technical coverage and gives you the opportunity to broaden your experience across a variety of operational environments.

About the team
Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

title: Software Development Engineer, DynamoDB Index and Search
descriptionHtml:
Software Development Engineer — DynamoDB Indexing

Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless, distributed NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at virtually any scale. DynamoDB's indexing infrastructure powers Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs), enabling customers to efficiently query their data across alternate access patterns without managing additional infrastructure.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to help design, build, and operate the distributed indexing infrastructure at the heart of DynamoDB. You will work on problems at the intersection of distributed systems, stream processing, storage engines, and large-scale data replication — ensuring that secondary indexes remain consistent, performant, and highly available as the underlying table data changes continuously.

The role includes designing and evolving the index replication pipeline that propagates mutations from base tables to secondary indexes in near-real time; building index lifecycle mechanisms that handle creation, backfill, compaction, rebalancing, and recovery across partitioned datasets at massive scale; and optimizing the storage, query, and cost efficiency of secondary indexes across all DynamoDB partitions and regions.

You will help determine how indexes are created, maintained, scaled, and recovered while the underlying DynamoDB data continues to change at millions of requests per second. You will also shape how indexing infrastructure integrates with DynamoDB's partitioning, replication, admission control, and query-processing systems — delivering predictable performance across latency, throughput, freshness, availability, and cost.

This is an opportunity to shape the future of DynamoDB's indexing capabilities — from foundational architecture through customer launch and operation at DynamoDB scale.

Key Job Responsibilities

- Design and implement distributed index replication infrastructure that propagates base-table mutations to Global Secondary Indexes with low latency and high fidelity.

- Build and optimize the Log Propagator pipeline, including log streaming, checkpointing, session management, admission control, and failure recovery across thousands of partitions.

- Develop index lifecycle mechanisms covering index creation, backfill from existing table data, incremental updates, compaction, partition splits and merges, rebalancing, and deletion — all while the table continues to serve live traffic.

- Ensure that secondary indexes remain consistent with the base table under concurrent writes, partition movements, leader elections, and failure scenarios, with well-defined freshness and consistency semantics.

- Integrate indexing infrastructure with DynamoDB's distributed storage, partitioning, replication, and query-processing systems, including StorageNode, Partition Manager, and the control plane.

- Design and build mechanisms for index availability and recovery, including handling degraded partitions, stuck replication sessions, and automated remediation of index lag.

- Optimize tradeoffs among replication latency, write amplification, storage efficiency, throughput, memory usage, and operational cost across the indexing fleet.

- Build observability, alarming, and operational tooling for the indexing pipeline — enabling rapid diagnosis and resolution of replication lag, backfill progress, and partition-level health.

- Drive operational excellence across the indexing fleet, including patching, deployment safety, capacity planning, and on-call processes for a Tier-1 service.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

You close the day translating cutting-edge robotics ambitions into resilient, secure AWS designs—always one step ahead of what autonomous machines will demand next.

title: Kernel/OS Engineer, EC2 Nitro Instance Lifecycle Management
descriptionHtml:
EC2 Core Compute drives the planet’s largest, fastest growing and most feature-rich compute cloud. Nitro is AWS’ ground-up design for virtualization at global scale built on a fully custom stack of hardware, firmware and applications. Nitro has enabled EC2 to support Intel, AMD and Amazon’s custom silicon - the Graviton processor family - while raising the industry bar for security and performance across our product line. We integrate hardware, firmware, application software and services to deliver new virtualized and bare-metal compute platforms for companies from startups through the Fortune 500.

As a skilled engineer with expertise in C, you'll work on software that provide essential services to customer instances and EC2 dataplane applications. This role offers unique opportunities to design and build high-performance, reliable services that operate at massive scale to ensure customers are able to launch instances successfully while simultaneously protecting droplet resources from potential security threats.

This position requires an engineer who thrives in an embedded systems environment and can deliver robust solutions for the infrastructure that underpins AWS services. You'll help shape the future of cloud computing by creating efficient, scalable, and secure services that operate close to the hardware. Your contributions will directly impact customer experience and the performance of one of the world's largest cloud platforms.


Key job responsibilities
- You will be responsible for designing, developing, testing, and deploying large-scale software running across AWS data centers.
- You will collaborate closely with EC2 teams to help curate the team’s roadmap. You will also drive the system architecture, spearhead best practices that enable a quality product, and help coach and develop junior engineers.
- A successful candidate will have an established background in engineering large scale software systems, a strong technical ability, great communication skills, and a motivation to achieve results in a fast paced environment.
- Openness to leveraging AI tools and technologies to enhance productivity and technical problem-solving.


A day in the life
Your day begins with a quick team standup to align on priorities and discuss any operational issues that need attention. You'll spend time designing new components for our embedded services or enhancing existing ones, writing efficient code in C or Rust, and collaborating with teammates on technical reviews. You might debug complex issues affecting service performance, optimize critical paths in the codebase, or work on improving security mechanisms. Throughout the day, you'll coordinate with partner teams to ensure smooth integration between services and regularly validate that your solutions meet the high reliability standards required for AWS infrastructure.



About the team
We play critical role in managing EC2 instances that utilize the Nitro system. We handle a diverse set of responsibilities related to the lifecycle, and hardware management of EC2 instances. The team owns key responsibilities that includes EC2 Instances life cycle management on the Nitro platform to manage instance creation, execution and termination by coordinating with other on-instance components such as Hypervisor, Networking and Storage services. We're passionate about solving challenging problems at the intersection of hardware and software, creating high-performance services that operate at massive scale.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- Professional experience working on the Linux Kernel
- Professional experience in C programming
- Proficient in at least one CPU architecture such as x86 or ARM
- Understanding of operating system internals

Preferred qualifications

- Extensive professional experience working on the Linux Kernel
- Extensive professional experience in C programming
- Professional experience working on a hypervisor, such as kvm, xen or hyper-v
- Solid understanding of performance-critical areas of the Linux Kernel

title: Systems Development Engineer, EC2 Core Platforms Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Build the systems that bring Amazon's newest servers to life. As a Systems Development Engineer on EC2 Core Platforms Engineering, you'll work at the seam between hardware and software to launch new compute platforms, keep the core fleet healthy at massive scale, and automate the way we build.

We own the quality, performance, and reliability of the platforms that host EC2 instances, from lab bring-up through general availability. You'll bring up and validate new EC2 server platforms, working hands-on with Nitro firmware, operating systems, and provisioning, then diagnose and reduce failures across the core fleet to drive reliability. A big part of the role is building the automation, including AI-driven tooling, that makes platform launches faster, safer, and more repeatable.

You'll collaborate across hardware engineering, Annapurna, and the Nitro component teams, working on some of the largest compute fleets in the world, where a single improvement in reliability or build automation compounds across millions of hosts.

Key job responsibilities
- Help bring up and validate new server platforms that host cloud compute instances, from early lab testing through production launch, working across firmware, operating systems, and hardware.

- Diagnose and reduce hardware and software failures across a large-scale server fleet, using a data-driven, methodical approach to find root causes and drive fixes that improve reliability.

- Build software and automation that streamline how new platforms are introduced, reducing manual effort in provisioning, deployment, and validation so platforms reach production faster and with a high quality bar.

- Develop solutions to difficult problems that span firmware, operating systems, networking, and infrastructure.

- Improve the safety, agility, and automation of the build and launch process, and share what you learn with the team.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 1+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 3+ years of administrative experience in networking, storage systems, operating systems and hands-on systems engineering experience

- Experience programming with at least one modern language such as C++, C#, Java, Python, Golang, PowerShell, Ruby

title: Logistics Program Mgr., AWS Cloud Logistics
descriptionHtml:
As a Transportation Operations Manager, you will serve as the connective tissue between operations execution and performance measurement across both logistics and warehousing services. You will own the full metrics lifecycle — from establishing goals and targets, to tracking performance, to reporting actuals vs. targets for stakeholders across the network. You will simultaneously drive day-to-day operations execution while identifying and implementing structural efficiency improvements that reduce cost, improve throughput, and elevate service levels.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES:

Metrics Framework & Goal Setting

Design and own the performance metrics framework for transportation and warehousing operations, establishing baseline targets, stretch goals, and tolerance thresholds across key indicators including on-time delivery, warehouse utilization, and carrier performance
Partner with Operations teams and senior leadership to align metrics targets with organizational objectives and network strategy goals
Build and maintain a unified scorecard spanning both logistics (carrier, lane, mode) and warehousing (throughput, labor, space utilization) dimensions, ensuring end-to-end supply chain visibility
Reporting & Actuals vs. Targets Tracking

Develop and publish recurring performance reports — daily, weekly, and monthly — tracking actuals against established targets and surfacing variance trends requiring intervention
Build automated reporting pipelines and dashboards that translate raw operational data into clear, actionable insights for operations managers and senior leadership
Own root cause analysis for metric deviations, documenting findings and driving corrective action plans with accountable stakeholders
Support QBR and MBR reporting cycles with structured narratives that contextualize performance trends against operational and market conditions
Operations Execution

Lead day-to-day transportation and warehousing operations execution, ensuring service continuity, compliance with SOPs, and alignment with carrier and LSP commitments
Serve as an escalation point for operational issues — carrier failures, capacity shortfalls, warehouse throughput bottlenecks — coordinating rapid resolution across internal teams and 3P providers
Operational Efficiency & Continuous Improvement

Identify inefficiencies across transportation lanes and warehousing operations through data analysis, and develop structured improvement initiatives with measurable outcomes
Build and maintain a continuous improvement pipeline — tracking initiative status, projected savings, and realized impact against plan
Develop supplier and carrier performance measurement frameworks that drive accountability and continuous improvement
Partner with category, procurement, and systems teams to align operational efficiency initiatives with broader network strategy and cost reduction goals
Stakeholder Alignment & Cross-functional Partnership

Align with building leadership, regional operations, Finance, and centralized procurement to ensure metrics and efficiency programs reflect both site-level realities and network-wide priorities
Develop relationships across the operations network to ensure best practices in reporting, tracking, and performance management are shared and implemented consistently


A day in the life
The day kicks off reviewing overnight carrier performance dashboards — two lanes missed on-time targets, triggering a root cause deep dive before 8am. By mid-morning, you're in a standup with LSP partners, working through a warehouse throughput bottleneck flagged in yesterday's actuals-vs-targets report. Lunch is spent refining an automated reporting pipeline ahead of next week's MBR. The afternoon brings a cross-functional call with systems and regional ops to align on Q3 efficiency targets. Before signing off, you're updating the continuous improvement tracker — one initiative just hit its projected performance milestone.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in supply chain management, engineering, business management or other relevant field
- 3+ years of program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or related field experience
- 5+ years of program or project management experience, or Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years of data analysis using tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, SQL, Tableau, or equivalent experience
- Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, or transportation or equivalent professional or military experience
- Experience communicating results to senior leadership, or experience in building financial and operational reports/data sets that inform business decision-making

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or MBA in supply chain, business, engineering, finance or related technical or quantitative field
- Experience in data centers, infrastructure service providers, or related technology companies
- 1+ years of using business intelligence reporting tools such as OBIEE, Business Objects, Cognos, Tableau, MicroStrategy, SSAS Cubes, etc. experience
- Experience with continuous improvement methods such as Kaizen, Lean, DMAIC, etc.
- Experience working in an operations, supply chain, transportation, project management or management consulting role
- Experience in procurement, supply chain, inventory management, contract management, lease administration or operations

title: Program Manager II, Delivery Quality & Process Integration, NA Grocery Delivery, SSD-G Delivery
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's NA Grocery Delivery team as a Program Manager, where you will serve as the central point of contact on the delivery team for driving initiatives that streamline upstream operations processes critical to Sub Same Day Grocery (SSD-G) delivery outcomes. In this role, you will bridge the gap between station operations, fulfillment processes, and last mile delivery, ensuring that upstream workflows are optimized to support delivery timeliness, order quality, and SLA compliance.

As the owner of SSD-G delivery process operations integration, you will identify and track KPIs across the end-to-end delivery pipeline, surface gaps where upstream process breakdowns drive downstream delivery defects, and work cross-functionally to design and implement solutions. This includes owning the identification of virtual-physical mismatches that create delivery failures, monitoring order damage and quality metrics, and driving accountability for key SLA compliance across partner teams. You will ideate, create, design, and drive completion of deliverables that structurally improve the connection between upstream operations and delivery outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and maintain the metrics framework that connects upstream process performance to SSD-G delivery outcomes.
- Serve as the delivery team's single-threaded POC for upstream operations partners, building relationships and driving alignment across teams.

- Drive deliverables end-to-end, from scoping and design through execution and sustained performance tracking.

title: Software Development Engineer Intern, Amazon University Talent Acquisition
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands.

Our Software Development Engineers (SDEs) use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDEs solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As an SDE-I, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers.

We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth.

Amazon internships across all seasons are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work in office, Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day. Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.

Key job responsibilities
Collaborate and communicate effectively with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to design, build, and operate innovative products and services that delight our customers, while participating in technical discussions to drive solutions forward.

Break down complex, ambiguous problems into well-defined, solvable components before implementation.

Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services, with distributed-systems scope varying by team.

Participate in code reviews as a core engineering practice, providing constructive feedback and validating correctness.

Contribute to clear and accurate technical documentation.

Use GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity, and critically validate, verify, and integrate AI-generated code, exercising sound judgement about when to trust AI output.

Write clean, maintainable code following best practices and design patterns.

Work in an agile environment practicing CI/CD principles while participating in operational responsibilities including on-call duties.

Demonstrate operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, and resolving production issues.

A day in the life
As an intern, you will be matched to a manager and a mentor and will have the opportunity to influence the evolution of Amazon technology and lead critical projects early in your career.

In addition to working on an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage with Amazonians for both personal and professional development, expand your network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship. No matter the location of your internship, we give you the tools to own your project and learn in a real-world setting.

Basic qualifications

- Are enrolled in or have completed a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, or majors relating to these fields

title: Analista de Qualidade UTR, First Mile
descriptionHtml:
Esta é uma posição de tempo integral, permanente, presencial baseada em ESA8 - Osasco, BR e não oferece benefícios de realocação. Os candidatos devem estar localizados e legalmente autorizados a trabalhar em Brazil para serem elegíveis para consideração.

Quer crescer profissionalmente, se desafiar e fazer história? Na Amazon, isso é possível. Nossas equipes de logística transformam, todos os dias, a maneira como nos conectamos com clientes ao redor do mundo, resolvendo grandes desafios da indústria.

No time de transporte da Amazon, garantimos que cada pacote – grande ou pequeno – chegue ao seu destino, cumprindo nossa promessa aos clientes.

A equipe de UTR First Mile é responsável por garantir a excelência operacional nas etapas iniciais da cadeia logística da Amazon no Brasil. Nesta posição, será responsável por monitorar, analisar e melhorar continuamente os processos operacionais de qualidade nos nodes de First Mile, garantindo a conformidade com os padrões da Amazon e impulsionando a experiência do cliente,

Se você busca desafios, crescimento e um ambiente que valoriza a inovação, essa pode ser a oportunidade certa para você!

A Amazon está comprometida com um ambiente de trabalho diverso e inclusivo. A Amazon é um empregador que oferece igualdade de oportunidades e não discrimina com base em raça, origem nacional, gênero, identidade de gênero, orientação sexual, status de veterano protegido, deficiência, idade ou outro status legalmente protegido.

● Participar de projetos de melhoria contínua e automação de processos, atraves do uso de IA
● Garantir a padronização de processos de qualidade em todos os nodes da rede First Mile
● Suportar o onboarding e treinamento de novos membros da equipe em processos e padrões de qualidade
● Viajar 40-50% do tempo para apoiar lançamentos no local e o envolvimento dos parceiros.

descriptionHtml:
We have an immediate opening for a Building Information Modeling Specialist in the Herndon, VA area

Are you an experienced BIM/CAD professional with a passion for data center design and looking for a challenge of contributing to BIM lifecycle management? Are you well versed in graphical communication for data center building drawings in all disciplines? If so, we are looking for you to help us make history.

As a Lifecycle BIM Specialist, you will produce and maintain Lifecycle sets for CSA and MEP drawing sets for our fleet of Data Centers. You will provide support to the Fleet Remediation Engineering team through preparation of computer generated CSA/MEP Lifecycle drawing sets ensuring that all as-built drawings are accurately updated. Your experience in Revit and AutoCAD will be utilized to update and create new BIM models from as-built documentation.

Your experience in Architectural, Structural, & Civil drawings is a plus but you will influence design & record documents for all Commercial/industrial Building Systems centering on MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, & Plumbing) for Air Handling Units, Cooling towers, Chillers, Controls, Fire Detection/Suppression, Plumbing & Piping, P&ID, elements of high, medium and low voltage transmission fundamentals, industrial electrical distribution, wire types and sizes, conduit types & configurations for riser and underground applications, as well as fiber optic and copper data/voice media types, details, elevations, & schedules.

You will help develop tools and procedures for standards compliance to streamline workflow and assist with reporting metrics for the GL team while providing support to the Fleet Remediation Engineering team through preparation of CSA/MEP Lifecycle drawing sets. You will provide support for this content through our Global Library as well as preforming on-site validation as needed. You should have experience producing and maintaining permit, construction, and record drawing sets for large facilities (Data Centers, Factories, Hospitals, etc.).

Each day you will interact with different teams responsible for engineering, development, integration, and operation of these complex technological sites.
