title: Sr. Solutions Architect, Advertising and Marketing
descriptionHtml:
AWS Global Sales drives adoption of the AWS cloud worldwide, enabling customers of all sizes to innovate and expand in the cloud. Our team empowers every customer to grow by providing tailored service, unmatched technology, and architecture guidance. We dive deep to understand each customer's unique challenges, then craft innovative solutions that accelerate their success. This customer-first approach is how we built the world's most adopted cloud. Join us and help us grow.

The Role
As a trusted customer advocate, Solutions Architects help organizations understand best practices around advanced cloud-based solutions, and provide advice on strategies for migrating existing workloads to the cloud. You’ll help drive successful business outcomes across a broad set of enterprise customers through your passion for educating, training, designing and building cloud solutions.

You will have the opportunity to help shape and execute a strategy to build deep adoption and broad use of AWS within your enterprise customers, and you will do this by mobilizing resources within AWS and working with our extensive partner network.

Key job responsibilities
- Communicate effectively with both business and technical stakeholders as a trusted technical advisor.
- Participate in deep architectural and design discussions to create world-class solutions built on AWS while ensuring solutions are designed for successful deployment in the cloud.
- Author and contribute to AWS customer-facing publications such as whitepapers and proof of concepts.
- In partnership with the sales team, formulate and execute a sales strategy to exceed revenue objectives through the adoption of AWS.
- Build deep relationships with business and senior technical individuals within customers to enable them to be cloud advocates.
- Capture and share best-practice knowledge amongst the AWS solutions architect community.
- Travel is expected to be 20%.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Data Center Capacity Delivery - Controls
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptable power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
Review quarterly maintenance results and action items for BMS/EPMS and drive resolution.
Develop project scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of effort (LOE) for customer requests.
Manage scope, schedule, finance, and execution of BMS/EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
Support procurement: RFQs/RFPs, RFI responses, vendor proposal reviews, and purchase orders.
Participate in the AWS global on-call schedule for immediate technical support to in-service data centers.
Attend project meetings, coordinate with project leaders, and report status to Controls management.
Support commissioning activities in data centers.
Review, implement, troubleshoot, and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO); provide design-team feedback.
Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables and navigate challenging situations.
Financially manage BMS/EPMS service contracts.
Locally visit assigned in-operation data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, and supervise vendor compliance with scope, design, SOO, and local codes.

descriptionHtml:

You operate with a high degree of independence, executing day-to-day operations autonomously and routinely delivering the right outcomes with limited guidance — even when project strategy is not yet well-defined. You deliver a mix of tactical and strategic initiatives that impact multiple teams and/or geographies in support of significant business objectives. You own design oversight, external partner selection, contract negotiations, and project procurement — and you are accountable for the full performance of your external project management partners, architects, design consultants, general contractors, and subcontractors.

Beyond project delivery, you contribute to developing Amazon's internal and external construction networks, drive best practices across the organization, and are learning to force multiply — elevating the performance of the teams and partners around you. title: InfraOps Support Engineer, Operations Management Center (OMC)
descriptionHtml:
The InfraOps Support Engineer is a Tier 1 support engineer in Amazon's Operations Management Center (OMC) - a 24/7/365 team that keeps the technology inside Amazon's 400+ corporate office buildings running across Networking, Audio-Visual (AV), and Print services. This engineer is the first line of response for office-infrastructure incidents.

Operating within the Amazon Support Engineer (SupEng) job family, the engineer provides high-quality support across all three service areas while beginning to develop deep subject-matter expertise in one or more focus areas, for which they become the technical point of contact on their team. They respond, triage and resolve incidents within target times using established procedures, detect trends before they become problems, contribute to and refine the team's operating procedures, and mentor more junior engineers. Success requires the ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative, shift-based environment.

Key job responsibilities
On a typical shift, an InfraOps Support Engineer will:

1. Monitor, Detect & Triage

Be the first line of response and keep ahead of problems.

Triage incoming incidents (tickets) within defined target response times, using judgment to resolve in place or route to the responsible team.

Use dashboards, alarms, and other tools for Networking, AV, and Print services across the global building fleet, interpreting what those signals indicate to solve incidents.

Detect ongoing trends or emerging problems before they occur and define proactive actions to prevent customer impact.

Assess incident scope and severity, correlate related incidents into a single parent incident, and prioritise work against SLAs.

2. Troubleshoot & Support

Resolve issues and support the team's products and systems.

Provide high-quality Tier 1 support for the products and systems in the team's scope, resolving straightforward problems with limited documentation and minimal escalation.

Support critical issues using existing runbooks; maintain composure through difficult interactions until the issue is resolved.

Perform on-call duties on a rotating schedule and respond to emergent events.

Escalate appropriately when resolution requires significant deviation from procedure or when an issue becomes a risk.

3. Subject-Matter Expertise & Technical Leadership

Grow into the go-to person for a focus area.

Develop and apply expertise in one or more focus areas (e.g., Networking, AV, or Print), acting as the technical point of contact for that area within the team.

Give technical direction to others and impart knowledge to users, customers, and teammates.

Lead internal team projects and deliver on defined goals and timelines.

4. Documentation & Operational Improvement

Improve how the team operates.

Identify areas to improve support documentation and processes, and author new runbooks/SOPs and knowledge-base articles where gaps exist.

Identify improvements to existing and new support tools that increase operational efficiency, and help drive their implementation.

Help develop and refine the operational policies and procedures used by the team.

5. Mentoring & Collaboration

Raise the bar for the team.

Serve as a mentor to junior engineers and act as a training buddy for new hires; may assist in hiring activities.

Maintain good working relationships across Amazon and work cross-functionally with partner teams to solve problems and improve processes.

Communicate infrastructure health and trends clearly, both in real time and as inputs to weekly/monthly business reviews.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working with Windows server technologies: AD, DFS, Print Services, SCCM
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
- Experience in IT client, server, and network service delivery
- Experience with networking technology (TCP/IP, subnetting, DNS and DHCP)
- Experience supporting Windows, Mac and/or Linux operating systems in a corporate setting
- Experience working in large-scale networking environments
- High school diploma, or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in computer networking
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in Network protocols like DNS/DHCP/TCP
- Experience supporting video-conference and teleconference equipment.

title: Sr Technical Program Manager, New Product Introduction, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world — designed with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve individual households, schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Software and hardware changes introduce complexity, requiring coordinated cut-in planning, effectivity control, and production impact assessment across the full vehicle build flow, from Contract Manufacturer through our Factory up to Launch Operations.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
This TPM will be a core member of Amazon Leo Production's New Product Introduction team, owning the Engineering Change Implementation process end-to-end. This complex value stream governs how engineering changes, spanning both software and hardware, are reviewed, and implemented across Leo's satellite manufacturing and test operations. The role requires a demonstrated ability to drive industrial and manufacturing readiness, ensuring that engineering changes are introduced into production in a controlled, scalable, and operationally sustainable manner. The role interfaces with procurement, finance, GSE, production, warehouse, satellite design engineering, and launch operations, and is based in Redmond, WA.

The scale and complexity of engineering change management demands coordinated activities across both daily urgent activities and long-term strategic initiatives. As an adept of "working yourself out of a job," this TPM will lead the critical process and tool improvements required to protect production stability while enabling rapid innovation cycles.

Program Ownership & Governance

* Hold single-threaded ownership of the Engineering Change Control programs, managing both software and hardware change streams across Leo manufacturing and test operations
* Manage the Engineering Change Implementation Board and Software Production Implementation mechanisms, ensuring structured intake, risk classification, and approval of all changes
* Maintain the single source of truth for the change schedule, developed collaboratively with stakeholders across production, test, quality, and operations
* Serve as the primary escalation point for production-impacting changes, coordinating rapid response to quality gaps and engineering-driven stoppages

descriptionHtml:

Role Overview
We are seeking an exceptional Software Development Engineer II to build the foundational systems and consumer-facing features that enable trustworthy AI experiences at scale. You will partner closely with our Principal Engineers and Managers to design and implement privacy-preserving AI architectures, responsible AI frameworks, and accessibility features that set the standard for consumer AI products.

This is a high-impact role where you'll tackle complex technical challenges at the intersection of AI innovation and customer trust—balancing performance with privacy, building explainable AI systems, and creating guardrails that protect customers while enabling delightful experiences.


Key job responsibilities
What You'll Build

Privacy-Preserving AI Systems:
* Design and implement federated learning and differential privacy techniques for on-device and hybrid AI architectures

Technical Excellence: You have strong computer science fundamentals and practical experience building distributed systems. You write clean, maintainable code and establish best practices that enable your team to move fast without breaking things.

Bias for Action: You thrive in ambiguous environments where you need to make pragmatic trade-offs between innovation and safety. You ship iteratively and learn from customer feedback.

Inclusive Mindset: You design systems that work for all customers, considering diverse abilities, contexts, and use cases from the start rather than as an afterthought.

title: Data Center Security Specialist, CMH-Plain City
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) serves customers and developers who rely on storage, compute, and our other service capabilities. Our customers trust us to handle their data with air-tight security measures, which is something that we guarantee.

AWS is growing rapidly, and we are looking for a Data Center Security Specialist (DSS) to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team, who will help manage and improve site security operations in our data centers.

Key job responsibilities
The selected individual will be responsible for managing physical security operations, developing post orders, defining security procedures, handling site incidents, working with security equipment, participating in construction projects and to drive day-to-day process improvement activities and managing vendors.

Duties include ensuring consistent deployment of all required security policies and procedures and participate in re-occurring site audits and reviews and testing new security technologies.
Must have and demonstrate resilient leadership skills, flexibility to work in dynamic environment, exceptional knowledge of security practices and strong written and verbal communication.

A day in the life
A day typically begins with a comprehensive review of any security incidents or operational issues that occurred. They start their duties by conducting thorough security system checks, including testing access control systems, verifying camera operations, and reviewing alarm panel statuses.

Throughout the day, they actively participate in operations meetings with the DC Operations team to align on maintenance activities, review vendor access requests, and address any emerging security concerns. They conduct detailed facility walkthroughs, inspecting perimeter security, checking equipment condition, and documenting any vulnerabilities in the security tracking system.

A significant portion of their day involves managing security-related tickets, including processing badge access requests, coordinating vendor escorts, and handling security system maintenance requests. They take ownership of vendor management activities, overseeing the security guard force operations, verifying SLA compliance, and conducting random post inspections to ensure quality service delivery.

The specialist regularly participates in security team meetings where they review metrics, discuss process improvements, and coordinate upcoming projects. They dedicate time to administrative responsibilities such as updating security procedures, completing required reports, reviewing camera footage, and documenting incidents as needed.

descriptionHtml:

title: Principal Design Technologist, AWS Search, Security, Observability, & Governance
descriptionHtml:
Are you the person who makes a bold interaction idea technically real? AWS is looking for a Principal Design Technologist to serve as technical advisor for AWS SSOG (Security, Search, Observability & Governance).

You'll sit at the center of a self-learning intelligence flywheel: our Delight Lab validates novel interaction models — graduated autonomy, step-level replay, policy-check loops — and you make them real, stress-testing them through high-fidelity prototypes and landing them as production-ready components in our Rhythm design system on AWS Core. This is a deep-craft builder role with outsized leverage: every pattern you prove out compounds across the portfolio. If you live in the codebase, think in systems, and want your prototypes to become the standard the whole org ships against, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Serve as the Director of Design's technical advisor on innovation: judge which novel interaction models emerging from Delight Lab are worth betting on, and chart the path to make them real.
- Push the frontier of agentic interaction design — graduated autonomy, step-level replay, policy-check loops — proving out ideas no one has shipped yet through high-fidelity, working prototypes.
- Invent the patterns, not just implement them: originate new interaction models and reusable components where none exist, and set the technical standard for what "state of the art" means across SSOG.
- Turn breakthrough prototypes into production-ready Rhythm components on AWS Core, so every validated innovation compounds across six products and counting instead of being re-solved.
- Build the connective tissue of the innovation flywheel, the tooling and systems that let the team sense, synthesize, and scale emerging interaction patterns faster.
- De-risk the boldest bets: stress-test feasibility early so the org can commit to ambitious ideas with confidence rather than retreating to safe ones.
- Raise the innovation bar of the entire design org through prototypes, patterns, and pairing, making everyone around you braver and more technical.

A day in the life
Your morning might start in Delight Lab's latest findings — a graduated-autonomy model that tested well — and by mid-morning you're building a working prototype to pressure-test whether it holds up technically, not just in a research setting. After lunch, you're pairing with design-system engineering to turn an approval-gate pattern you proved last week into a production Rhythm component, so every team gets it for free. Later, you're in a working session with the Director of Design, giving a direct read on which emerging interaction models are feasible, which need another pass, and what it'll take to ship them. This team builds in production, not in Figma — and your prototypes are how the org decides what's real.

About the team
We're the SSOG Transformers design team, shaping how builders experience AWS Security, Search, Observability & Governance. We operate as an AI-native builder team running a self-learning intelligence flywheel: our internal design research practice (Delight Lab) senses and validates how people and AI actually collaborate — when they hand off control, when autonomy should be earned through evidence — Design Brain helps us synthesize those signals, and Rhythm scales the proven patterns into a production design system on AWS Core. We don't hand off specs and wait. We prototype, commit production code, run experiments, and compound every validated pattern across six products and counting. If you want your technical craft to set the standard the whole org builds on, this is the team to join.

Basic qualifications

- A demonstrable portfolio of shipped, production-grade interfaces you built — not just prototyped — for complex, data-dense technical products (observability, security, developer tools, or cloud infrastructure).
- Expert front-end engineering ability: you build high-fidelity, interactive prototypes and commit production code (React/TypeScript, HTML/CSS), and partner with engineering as a peer in the codebase.
- Experience building and maintaining design-system components at scale, architecture, accessibility, and cross-team adoption.
- Experience translating novel, ambiguous interaction concepts into technically validated, shippable patterns.
- Experience operating at Staff/Principal level (or equivalent) as a design technologist, creative technologist, or design engineer at a top-tier technology company.
- A track record of influence as a technical advisor or force-multiplier across teams, raising others' craft through prototypes, tooling, and example rather than direct authority alone.

Preferred qualifications

- Hands-on experience prototyping AI/ML and agentic experiences — autonomous agents, human-in-the-loop, progressive/graduated autonomy, step-level replay, policy-check loops.
- Experience building the tooling or systems that let a team sense, synthesize, and scale interaction patterns (design-intelligence pipelines, pattern libraries, instrumentation).
- Direct experience in observability, security, search, or governance product domains.
- Experience taking research or lab findings and operationalizing them into a production design system.
- Proficiency with AI-assisted design and build tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Kiro, v0).
- Published thought leadership or recognized open-source/community contributions in design engineering.

title: Electrical Integration Leader - Power Distribution & Infrastructure, OMHS
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking an Electrical Installation Lead – Power Distribution & Infrastructure to drive the successful installation of electrical power systems for automation and material handling equipment across multiple greenfield and brownfield fulfillment center sites. This role provides field-based electrical installation leadership focused specifically on heavy wire pulls, power distribution infrastructure, conduit and raceway systems, control panel placement, and high-voltage terminations in complex industrial environments. The Electrical Installation Lead – Power Distribution will directly manage installation crews
responsible for all electrical infrastructure that feeds power to MHE systems. This includes
conduit installation from Main Distribution Panels (MDPs) to sub-panels and equipment, cable tray routing, heavy wire pulling (480V 3-phase), control panel placement, disconnect installation, junction box and pull box placement, grounding systems, and wire terminations. You will ensure all power distribution work is executed safely, in compliance
with NEC/NFPA codes, and to Amazon's quality and schedule standards. This role reports to the Site Deployment Manager and works in close coordination with the Low Voltage Devices & Controls lead — your team must complete power infrastructure in each zone before device installation crews can mobilize. This sequencing makes schedule discipline and quality critical to overall project success.

Key job responsibilities
Power Distribution Installation Leadership:
• Lead and manage electrical installation crews focused on power distribution infrastructure for MHE systems across North American facilities
• Oversee conduit and raceway installation from Main Distribution Panels (MDPs) to sub-panels, disconnects, and equipment locations
• Manage heavy wire pulling operations through conduit including 480V 3-phase power feeders, ensuring proper cable sizing, labeling, and termination
• Direct control panel placement and mounting at designated locations per engineering drawings, ensuring proper clearance and accessibility
• Oversee installation of cable tray systems, junction boxes, pull boxes, and wireways
• Manage installation of disconnects, motor starters, overloads, and related power distribution components
• Direct grounding system installation and bonding connections per NEC requirements
• Ensure proper wire terminations with correct torque values, lugging, and labeling at all connection points
• Oversee cable management including wire bundling, cable supports, strain relief,
and routing compliance

Drawing Interpretation & Field Execution:
• Review and interpret electrical drawings including one-line diagrams, panel schedules, conduit schedules, cable schedules, and electrical installation details
• Verify field installation matches engineering drawings and identify conflicts requiring resolution
• Partner with engineering teams to clarify drawings, resolve field conflicts, and validate installation intent
• Maintain accurate field documentation including redlines, punch lists, installation status reports, and turnover documentation
• Coordinate with mechanical installation teams on shared routing paths, penetrations, and structural supports

Quality, Safety & Compliance
• Ensure all electrical power distribution work is completed in accordance with NEC/NFPA codes, project specifications, and Amazon standards
• Perform and oversee quality inspections on conduit installations, wire pulls, terminations, panel connections, and grounding systems
• Verify conduit fill ratios, bend radius compliance, and proper support spacing per code requirements
• Manage electrical punch list identification and repair for all power infrastructure scope
• Drive achievement of safety, timeline, cost, and quality metrics across assigned zones
• Ensure lockout/tagout compliance and electrical safety practices during all installation activities

Coordination & Communication
• Coordinate electrical infrastructure installation with mechanical teams, controls engineering, construction, vendors, and operations stakeholders
• Manage zone handoff sequencing with the Low Voltage Devices & Controls lead — power infrastructure must be complete before device installation begins
• Track electrical installation progress, risks, blockers, and quality issues, escalating when support is needed
• Participate in project-level technical reviews, installation readiness reviews, and punch walks
• Manage relationships with electrical contractors, OEMs, vendors, and internal project stakeholders
• Participate in daily business reviews with installation progress updates
• Support development and continuous improvement of electrical installation standards, field checklists, and scalable deployment processes

A day in the life
Your day starts at the site coordination meeting where you review which zones have completed mechanical steel installation and are ready for electrical infrastructure mobilization. You walk the floor with your conduit crew — verifying raceway runs from MDPs to sub-panels against engineering drawings, checking conduit supports and fill
ratios, and confirming proper routing around obstructions. You oversee wire pulling operations in active zones, ensuring proper cable sizing, bend radius compliance, and pull tension limits are respected. Mid-morning you inspect control panel placements, verifying mounting locations match drawings, checking clearance requirements, and confirming grounding connections. You validate junction box and disconnect installations, review wire terminations for proper torque values and labeling, and address any field conflicts that require engineering clarification. By afternoon, you're tracking installation progress against the schedule, coordinating with the device installation lead on upcoming zone handoffs, and documenting redlines for as-built updates. You close out at the daily business review with progress updates and flag any material or access risks for the next
day.

About the team
The OMHS Installation & Deployment team supports the deployment and integration of automation and material handling systems across Amazon's operations network. The team works cross-functionally with engineering, construction, operations, supply chain, vendors, and field execution partners to deliver safe, scalable, and reliable systems.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in engineering including a supervisory role managing people
- Experience in a fast-paced, automated, industrial, logistics, production or manufacturing environment
- 5+ years of experience in industrial electrical installation, electrical construction,
- power distribution, or a similar technical environment
- Experience leading or supervising electrical installation crews, contractors, or field execution teams
- Experience reading and interpreting electrical drawings including one-line diagrams, panel schedules, conduit schedules, and wiring diagrams
- Experience with industrial power distribution systems including 480V 3-phase, motor control circuits, disconnects, and related infrastructure
- Experience with conduit installation, raceway systems, cable tray, wire pulling, and termination practices
- Experience working in fast-paced industrial, logistics, manufacturing, or construction environments
- Ability to travel up to 50% domestically; travel may exceed 50% in some instances with short notice

Preferred qualifications

- Prior experience managing journeyman electricians, electrical contractors, or industrial electricians on large-scale installation projects
- Prior experience working for a material handling integrator
- Prior experience installing power distribution infrastructure for conveyor or sortation systems
- Experience with 480V 3-phase systems, motor control centers (MCCs), VFD power wiring, and transformer installations
- Journeyman electrician license, master electrician license, or state electrical license
- Knowledge of AutoCAD Electrical, Bluebeam, BIM 360, or equivalent drawing review software
- Experience with NEC/NFPA compliance in industrial or construction environments
- Experience managing third-party electrical contractors and subcontractors
- Experience with punch list management, redlines, installation quality inspections, and turnover documentation
- Lean, Six Sigma, PMP, or related project management certifications

title: Sr. Customer Solutions Manager, AGS Brazil FSI
descriptionHtml:
As an AWS Customer Solutions Manager, you'll guide customers through their multi-year cloud transformation journey, ensuring seamless collaboration across AWS teams to deliver measurable business outcomes. You'll serve as a trusted advisor, orchestrating strategy and execution while solving complex cloud adoption challenges at scale.

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with customers to understand their cloud adoption goals and guide them through each phase of their transformation journey, from initial planning through operational excellence.
- Coordinate across AWS teams to ensure aligned execution, breaking down silos between sales, support, solutions architecture, and professional services to deliver integrated customer solutions.
- Develop and manage customer engagement plans that translate strategic objectives into actionable milestones, tracking progress and adjusting approaches based on business outcomes.
- Lead customer business reviews and executive briefings that communicate progress, address challenges, and identify opportunities for expanded AWS adoption and innovation.
- Identify and advocate for new AWS services and solutions that address customer needs, bringing creative approaches and tools to solve complex technical and operational challenges.

A day in the life
In this role, you'll work directly with customers navigating their cloud adoption, helping them understand the operational, educational, and governance aspects of their AWS journey. You'll coordinate across multiple AWS teams—including sales, support, solutions architecture, and professional services—to plan and support large-scale workload migrations. Your day might include translating strategic customer initiatives into executable plans, leading business reviews and executive briefings, or facilitating knowledge-sharing sessions that align technical solutions with business goals. You'll also identify opportunities to introduce new AWS services and tools that address emerging customer challenges, working collaboratively with your peers to drive innovation and operational excellence.

About the team
We're a global team dedicated to helping customers succeed in their cloud transformation. Our vision is to make cloud adoption accessible, efficient, and impactful for organizations of all sizes. We work closely with customers across industries, understanding their unique business challenges and helping them unlock the full potential of cloud technology. You'll collaborate with a diverse group of technical experts, account leaders, and customer teams who are committed to delivering exceptional outcomes. We value inclusive perspectives, continuous learning, and a culture where everyone contributes to our shared success. Our team embraces flexibility and supports a healthy balance between work and personal life, recognizing that our best work happens when we're energized and supported both professionally and personally.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Mental Health and Well-Being (MHW), Glamazon, and Women at Amazon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, management, or technology, or Bachelor's degree in business administration, finance, economics, computer science, data science, engineering, or other related field
- Experience in customer-facing work, engaging with customer executives, technologists or partners to solve business problems with advanced technologies
- Experience leading large-scale, technical or engineering programs with a proven record of thought leadership, business case development, realizing customer benefits, and successful program completion experience

Preferred qualifications

- PMP certification, or SCRUM/Agile, SAFe certification
- Experience implementing cloud services including migrations and modernization projects or similar

Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. title: Finance Manager, Fulfillment by Amazon - AI Native Finance Analytics & Controls
descriptionHtml:
Fulfillment By Amazon (FBA) Finance is seeking a Finance Manager who can do two things simultaneously: ensure the integrity of Amazon's largest seller fee revenue base AND turn that clean data foundation into profitability intelligence that drives fee strategy decisions.

This is not a traditional finance role — it's a hybrid that combines end-to-end FBA analytics and how we protect our fee revenue base, heavily powered by AI and automation,

You will own the connection between FBA fee revenue at the shipment level and operational costs across Amazon's fulfillment network — producing the fee-level P&L that tells leadership whether we're happy or sad with FBA economics and that our financial controls are working. You'll also own the GL reconciliation, revenue assurance, and quarterly inspection mechanisms that ensure those numbers are trustworthy. The controllership work is the foundation; the analytics work is the payoff.
This role sits at the intersection of all fee verticals, providing the consolidated profitability view that no single vertical can see alone. You'll partner across FP&A, Fee Strategy, Fee Technology, and Accounting.

The vision: Within 6 months, 80%+ of the controllership inspection work is automated through AI agents and intelligent workflows. Your time shifts from manual reconciliation to proactive anomaly detection, cross-fee profitability analysis, and producing the analytics that shape FBA's fee strategy.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end fee-level P&L: connect FBA revenue (by fee type, ASP band, size tier) to operational costs across the fulfillment network
- Build and maintain AI-powered variance decomposition and profitability reporting across fee activities (Supply Chain, Storage, Selling, Value Recovery)
- Perform key GL reconciliations to ensure complete, accurate, and timely financial reporting across multiple marketplaces
- Design and automate controllership inspection mechanisms — shifting from reactive audit to proactive, AI-driven anomaly detection
- Partner with Fee Strategy, Accounting, and Fee Technology teams to ensure fees are accurate, timely, and aligned with seller communication and internal strategy
- Deliver recurring revenue analytics with proactive signals for leadership; produce cross-fee margin analysis that informs fee strategy decisions
- Build AI agents and automated workflows targeting significant automation of routine controllership inspections — develop repeatable patterns the broader finance team can adopt
- Perform recurring and ad-hoc audits of fee revenues; manage seller transaction adjustments and revenue assurance
- Provide support for external/internal audit inquiries; act as subject matter expert for controllership and FBA profitability analytics


A day in the life
Your morning starts with an AI-generated anomaly report you built — replacing hours of manual reconciliation. You investigate a fee variance, trace it to a calculation edge case, and partner with Fee Tech to resolve it before close. By afternoon, you're building the monthly fee-level P&L, decomposing variances into rate and mix effects, and drafting the narrative for leadership. Between deep dives, you're refining automated workflows that turn weekly controllership checks from multi-hour manual pulls into minutes-with-exceptions. You hold both lenses — "are the numbers right?" and "what do they mean?" — which makes you the person leadership trusts for both.

About the team
You will be joining a high-performing, fast-paced Finance team whose mission is to be the trusted strategic advisor to the business, driving profitable growth and scale through innovation. Is a highly visible role within the finance team and requires a strong leader and open communicator. You will have direct impact on top and bottom lines with the ability to deliver improvements for our teams. You will be part of a growing, fast paced, and fun team. You will have ownership for the implementation of your work and you will see direct business improvements based on the results of your work.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of finance, accounting, or related analytical field experience
- Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, tax, economics, or a related analytical field
- 5+ years of leading cross-functional initiatives that drive financial performance and strategy experience
- 5+ years of dissecting financial data and identifying patterns that support business strategy experience

Preferred qualifications

- 6+ years of identifying incomplete or inaccurate data, identifying the root cause and creating/implementing an escalation plan experience
- 6+ years of solving complex business challenges by delivering accurate and timely financial models, analysis, and recommendations that have a proven impact on business (e.g., financial savings, operational improvements, or customer benefits) experience

- Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (examples: SQL, MS Access, Essbase, Cognos) and other financial systems (examples: Oracle, SAP, Lawson, JD Edwards)

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Design Engineering
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to join our GDSCM team, focusing on the Basis of Design (BOD) and Programmatic Design Change Management (PDCM) programs. This role requires deep technical expertise across multiple engineering disciplines and the ability to evaluate complex design changes across 300+ in-flight projects.

As a Technical Program Manager, you will serve as a technical expert evaluating design change requests across electrical, mechanical, civil, structural, architectural, controls, plumbing, fire protection, and thermal systems. You will conduct feasibility analyses, coordinate technical reviews with principal engineers across all disciplines, and manage the end-to-end lifecycle of design changes from initiation through implementation.

You will work closely with Design Engineering, Construction Management, Procurement, Finance, and Product teams to ensure design changes are properly vetted, funded, and executed.

Key job responsibilities
Technical Design Evaluation
• Evaluate complex design changes across multiple engineering disciplines including electrical power distribution, mechanical cooling systems, structural loads, civil site work, architectural layouts, controls systems, plumbing infrastructure, and fire protection systems
• Analyze technical specifications, construction drawings, equipment datasheets, and system integration requirements to assess design change feasibility and impact
• Understand and explain the complexity of data center designs including power distribution from utility to rack level, cooling system architectures, backup power systems, and building infrastructure
• Identify technical dependencies and cross-discipline impacts when evaluating proposed design changes
• Assess constructability, maintainability, and operational implications of design modifications
• Review and validate technical calculations including electrical load calculations, cooling capacity requirements, structural load analysis, and hydraulic calculations
Design Change Management
• Manage portfolio of design changes across multiple in-flight projects, ensuring alignment with business priorities and technical requirements
• Conduct feasibility analyses and production readiness assessments for proposed design changes, evaluating technical risk, schedule impact, and cost implications
• Coordinate technical reviews with principal engineers across mechanical, electrical, structural, civil, architectural, controls, plumbing, and fire protection disciplines
• Develop and maintain implementation plans, tracking design change execution from approval through site deployment
• Present design change recommendations and cost implications to senior leadership, clearly articulating technical complexity and business impact
• Evaluate design improvements and innovations, assessing their applicability across the global portfolio
Cross-Discipline Collaboration
• Partner with Electrical Engineers on power distribution design, generator sizing, UPS configurations, switchgear specifications, and high-voltage systems
• Collaborate with Mechanical Engineers on cooling system design, HVAC configurations, piping layouts, and thermal management strategies
• Work with Structural Engineers on foundation design, seismic requirements, equipment support structures, and building loads
• Engage with Civil Engineers on site grading, stormwater management, utility routing, and site infrastructure
• Coordinate with Architectural teams on building layouts, space planning, and building envelope design
• Interface with Controls Engineers on building management systems, monitoring systems, and automation strategies
• Partner with Fire Protection Engineers on fire suppression systems, detection systems, and life safety requirements
Stakeholder Coordination
• Partner with Design Management teams to understand project-specific requirements, constraints, and technical challenges
• Collaborate with Finance teams on cost validation, funding strategies, and budget tracking for design changes
• Work with Construction Management and Procurement teams to assess schedule impacts, supply chain constraints, and constructability
• Engage with Product and Solutions teams to evaluate new equipment, emerging technologies, and design approaches
• Coordinate with Commissioning teams to ensure design changes support testing and startup requirements
Process Improvement
• Identify opportunities to streamline design change workflows and reduce execution timelines while maintaining technical rigor
• Develop and maintain technical documentation including standard operating procedures, design standards, technical specifications, and RACI matrices
• Contribute to automation initiatives and tooling improvements for design change management
• Support integration of cost validation frameworks and bulk funding mechanisms
• Drive continuous improvement in technical review processes and design quality standards
Program Execution
• Track and report on design change metrics including approval timelines, cost avoidance, implementation status, and technical quality
• Maintain design change databases and dashboards for cross-functional visibility
• Support BOD release planning and coordination to minimize redesign impacts
• Participate in weekly leadership reviews presenting program status, key decisions, and technical recommendations

About the team
The Global Design Standards and Change Management (GDSCM) organization within Data Center Engineering is responsible for establishing and maintaining design standards across the global data center portfolio. Our team manages three mission-critical programs:

Basis of Design (BOD) Establishes and governs the foundational technical standards for all global data center designs, ensuring consistency and quality across the portfolio.
Programmatic Design Change Management (PDCM) Manages design change requests across 300+ in-flight projects.
360 Equipment Qualification Program (360 EQP) Qualifies equipment and technologies for deployment across the global portfolio, evaluating emerging solutions and driving standardization of critical systems.

Together, these programs deliver capacity across the AMER, APAC, and EMEA regions.

Why AWS
o Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
o Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
o We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
o Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
o We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience in technical product or program management
- Experience working directly with engineering teams
- Experience in industrial or commercial engineering or project management in Mission Critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation, or oil/gas facilities
- Experience with Programmatic Design Change Management (PDCM) or design change management in infrastructure/construction environments

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or STEM, or 8-10+ years of equivalent experience in a related field
- Experience in data center operations or critical infrastructure operations
- Familiarity with the end-to-end design lifecycle for physical infrastructure (electrical, mechanical, civil, structural)

descriptionHtml:

You'll follow standard procedures, work through assigned tasks as priorities shift during the day, and focus on accuracy and quality in every transaction. Your lead sets the day's priorities, and you move between tasks as they shift. Some days you're building new hire kits for Monday onboarding. Other days you're processing returned assets, restocking vending machines across campus, or helping with a bulk removal from a decommissioned floor. You follow standard procedures, flag issues to your lead, update ServiceNow, and make sure every asset is accounted for. Your accuracy helps make sure every Amazonian has the equipment they need on Day 1.

About the team

You'll work alongside engineers, technicians, and operations specialists who build their own tools, write their own procedures, and own their programs end-to-end. Our culture is hands-on, direct, and team-first. We value people who take ownership, communicate clearly, and look for ways to improve how things work. Every day brings something different.

title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, Trainium Systems
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to build the software systems that turn a rack of AI accelerators from inert silicon into a system a customer can run workloads on? Do you want deep ownership of a service that every one of those systems depends on to boot, run, and stay healthy?

Who are we?
Annapurna Labs is the part of Amazon that designs the custom silicon behind the cloud, including Trainium for AI training, Graviton CPUs, and the AWS Nitro system. Nearly every server in AWS runs hardware we designed. We build the chips, the systems, and the software that power some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world.

What do we do?
We build the software that provisions, operates, updates, and monitors the servers behind AWS's largest AI training workloads, built on Trainium, Graviton, and the AWS Nitro system. We give the people who run this hardware a complete way to stand it up, watch its health, deliver new software to it, and diagnose it, all through open, standard interfaces. We own that software from design through the running system.

Why it's high-impact?
The hardware is just silicon until our software makes it provisionable, observable, and serviceable. Every system runs through what we build. The service you own is on the path for all of them, and the people who run this hardware depend on it every day.

What's the challenge?
There are many ambiguous and difficult challenges in our fast-moving space. Our services require deep system and software expertise. You need to have the ability to work within a fast moving and startup-like environment in a large company. You will identify solutions, trying ideas, given space to fail and iterate to produce products that your customers love.

What you will do?
You will be part of a team that builds services end to end, from a blank page to an operator running it in production. You work backward from what the customer needs, build on the interfaces the hardware teams expose, and set the requirements those teams meet for you.

Who would succeed in this role?
A deeply technical engineer who stays close to both the customer and the system design. You dive deep to understand how the hardware and the software actually behave, you decide when a small change is enough and when a problem needs a new design, and you own your service without waiting to be told. You raise the bar in code reviews and you lift the engineers around you.

Key job responsibilities
- Own building provisioning services end to end that bring a server from power-on to ready-to-run.
- Build the services or interfaces for monitoring, health, and anomaly detection that surface a server's state and flag a failing component before it takes a workload down.
- Develop the software-delivery service that pushes an update to a running server, verifies it, and recovers the server cleanly when an update fails.
- Develop the diagnostics and troubleshooting tools that let an operator isolate a fault without pulling in the team that built the service.
- Define the standard interfaces an operator's tools drive, and set the behavior the hardware teams deliver against them, including plugins, libraries, tools, or APIs.
- Build the integrations with standard orchestration stacks.
- Develop and build the services that let an operator run a fleet of these servers at scale.

A day in the life
You design and build the provisioning and management surface over standard interfaces like Redfish, and the boot flow operator tools drive. You build the offline software-update service and prove the signed bundle applies and recovers cleanly. You design each system against the interfaces the platform exposes and turn architecture decisions into APIs and tools a customer runs without you in the loop.

About the team
Our team builds the software suite for provisioning, monitoring, software delivery, and the diagnostics of Trainium systems, and we build all of it on open, standard interfaces. We serve the engineers and operators who run large-scale AI training and need to provision, monitor, update, and troubleshoot it on their own terms. We own it end to end.

We're a small team with a large charter. You own real systems on day one. There are no layers between you and the problem. You build it, you ship it, you operate it, you improve it.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Your core focus will be designing mechanisms and frameworks, driving process improvements, and taking projects from concept through to execution. At Amazon, you'll work alongside the latest AI and GenAI tools that are increasingly woven into how teams operate: from AI-powered capabilities that accelerate decision-making, to Generative AI that helps you focus on work that truly matters. A big part of your day involves driving change management. You will assess operational readiness for upcoming changes, engage stakeholders to evaluate risks, and coordinate approval workflows. In the afternoon, you might deep-dive into data to set up quantitative success metrics for a new initiative, prepare a business state report for senior leadership, or coach a junior team member through a complex stakeholder conversation. Collaboration happens in both Japanese and English, so you will regularly switch between the two as you work with local DSP partners and global teams.

Tworzenie, nadzorowanie i promowanie kultury bezpieczeństwa i zadowolenia z pracy
Analizowanie i wdrażanie modyfikacji w celu zapewnienia jakości i wydajności na stałym, wysokim poziomie
Nadzorowanie projektów mających na celu usprawnienie procesów, optymalizację wydajności i podniesienie jakości usług dla klientów w obrębie swojego obszaru odpowiedzialności
Analizowanie wydajności zmiany w stosunku do stosownych celów biznesowych i wprowadzanie działań mających na celu osiągnięcie doskonałości operacyjnej
Współpraca z innymi managerami w celu standaryzacji procesów na zmianach



A day in the life
Osoba na tym stanowisku pracuje w systemie zmianowym w jednym z naszych centrów logistycznych, zapewniając jego najwyższą możliwą wydajność. Głównym zadaniem Area Managera jest kierowanie i napędzanie kultury bezpieczeństwa oraz utrzymywanie jakości i standardów wydajności na zmianach. Area Manager nadzoruje również usprawnienia procesów w swoim obszarze i napędza ich wdrażanie. Typowy dzień jest tutaj niezwykle zróżnicowany i obejmuje rozmaite czynności, od rutynowego zarządzania zespołem i codziennych obowiązków operacyjnych, po doskonalenie procesów i szeroko zakrojone zadania operacyjne w sytuacjach awaryjnych. Osoba ta jest również mentorem dla nowych managerów.


About the team
Centrum logistyczne to miejsce, w którym firma Amazon stawiała swoje pierwsze kroki. Ze skromnego zespołu sprzedawców książek przekształciło się ono w wysokorozwiniętą korporację o zasięgu ogólnoświatowym, która każdego dnia obsługuje ponad 1,5 miliona zamówień. Osoby pracujące w centrach logistycznych stanowią fundament naszej działalności, a ich wysiłki pomagają nam w ekspansji naszej firmy na nowe rejony oraz w rozszerzeniu wachlarza świadczonych przez nas usług. Korzystając z najnowszych technologii, stale poszukujemy sposobów na zwiększenie i udoskonalenie gamy oferowanych przez nas produktów – dostarczanych szybko i tanio.
Nasze zespoły w centrach logistycznych są pierwszym ogniwem w łańcuchu dostaw przyczyniającym się do realizacji zamówień klientów w tempie, z którego tak słyniemy. Pracujemy w centrach logistycznych, które stanowią serce prężnej sieci operacyjnej firmy Amazon i określane są niekiedy jako „pierwszy kilometr”, ponieważ to właśnie tutaj większość przesyłek rozpoczyna swoją podróż. Pomagamy również zarządzać dynamicznie zmieniającymi się składami magazynowymi i umożliwiamy realizację szybkich dostaw 24 godziny na dobę.
W naszych centrach logistycznych pracuje wiele różnych osób, bo oferujemy perspektywy dla osób o każdym poziomie umiejętności i wykształcenia. Niektórzy z nas zajmują się bezpośrednio towarami, inni analizują dane, pomagając wszystkim w firmie w podejmowaniu trafnych decyzji.

Minimalne wynagrodzenie podstawowe dla tego stanowiska jest wymienione poniżej. Jako firma oferująca całościowe wynagrodzenie, pakiet Amazon może obejmować dodatkowe składniki wynagrodzenia, takie jak premia za podpisanie umowy oraz uprawnienie do uczestnictwa w programie ograniczonych jednostek akcyjnych (RSU) prowadzonym niezależnie przez Amazon.com Inc. w USA. Twój zespół rekrutacyjny podzieli się ostatecznym wynagrodzeniem podstawowym oraz wszelkimi odpowiednimi elementami całkowitego wynagrodzenia w zależności od umiejętności i wymagań.
Uznaniowe, dodatkowe świadczenia firmowe podlegają dalszym warunkom, w tym plany emerytalne, ubezpieczenie zdrowotne, ubezpieczenie na życie i od niezdolności do pracy, ubezpieczenie podróży służbowych, karta MultiSport, kod rabatowy dla pracowników i program (EDC/Extras), świadczenia dojazdowe tam, gdzie mają zastosowanie, oraz Program Wsparcia Pracowników (prywatne i poufne doradztwo oraz usługa skierowań wspierająca zdrowie i dobre samopoczucie).
Minimalne wynagrodzenie podstawowe dla tego stanowiska wynosi 9 683 PLN miesięcznie.

Basic qualifications

- Wykształcenie wyższe
- Wcześniejsze doświadczenie w kierowaniu zespołem
- Wcześniejsze doświadczenie w komunikacji z szerokim gronem partnerów biznesowych, w tym ze współpracownikami i z przełożonymi
- Umiejętność wykorzystywania danych analitycznych i empirycznych do podejmowania decyzji i rozwiązywania problemów
- Biegła znajomość języka angielskiego i polskiego w mowie i piśmie

title: Senior Program Manager, Amazon Scholars, Amazon Scholars
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Scholar team is seeking a Senior Program Manager to support the Amazon Scholar Program. This global, high-impact role supports a program that enables university professors to work on Amazon's most significant scientific and technical challenges without leaving their academic institutions through part-time or limited-term engagements.

The Senior Program Manager is responsible for facilitating key milestones across the Scholar employee lifecycle and for defining and delivering mechanisms and solutions that resolve complex problems, create lasting value and drive broad cross-organizational and cross-regional business impact.

This role supports a global program end-to-end — defining and executing development goals, consulting business and science leaders, developing a communication strategy, and managing all associated workflows. The Senior Program Manager builds internal mechanisms to automate and scale workflows globally and develops sustainable, long-term strategies for academic engagement.


Key job responsibilities
- **Process re-engineering and gap identification:** Identifies gaps and opportunities across regions, processes, and organizations (e.g., workflows, tooling, operating procedures). Serves as the single-threaded owner for a specialty employee model with non-standard lifecycle policies, part-time/limited-term engagement structures, and a unique compensation model. Owns a portfolio of critical workstreams to re-engineer processes, redefine ownership, and drive efficiency requiring cross-functional influence across central People eXperience and Technology (PXT) teams.

- **Mechanism design and adoption:** Creates, optimizes, and drives adoption of the mechanisms that ensure long-term program success. Builds novel mechanisms and artifacts to sustain the Scholar population, force-multiplying through stakeholders and partners while addressing unique use cases.

- **Autonomous leadership in ambiguous domains:** Operates with significant independence in areas where strategy has not yet been defined. Navigates high complexity and ambiguity with customers, stakeholders, and decision-makers that often include Amazon's most senior leadership. The Scholar Program team serves as an overlay across all core PXT functions — requiring strong judgment, backbone, and autonomy to prioritize roadmaps, invest resources, and deliver results.

- **Data-driven business operations:** Supports Business Operations for Scholars Programs, designing reporting to inspect key org goals, KPIs, and insights through MBRs and QBRs. Defines product requirements for dashboards and influences data availability and decision-making in partner teams — for example, working with Finance to enable mechanisms that track Scholar program spend as an input to business planning and ROI evaluation.


About the team
We are a team of strategic recruiters and program managers working to bring the best executive-level academic science talent to Amazon and elevate our reputation in the academic science community as an employer of choice. We believe Amazon is a unique place to measure the impact of new scientific ideas, given our scale and ownership of both an information infrastructure and a physical infrastructure. The Scholars Programs team focuses on three priorities:

1. Creating simple pathways to hire, develop, and retain world-class academic talent.
2. Developing internal and academic partnerships globally to address customer problems and demands.
3. Driving a non-conventional program to facilitate long-term science talent acquisition and retention in specialized domains.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- 5+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Knowledge of general AI tools
- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Experience building scalable programs and repeatable scalable processes, levering various tools and methods to create scale and efficiency
- Track record of building and scaling complex initiatives within fast-paced technology industry
- Experience with academic institutions or research organizations

title: Senior Cyber Operations Account Executive, Department of War (DoW)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Senior Cyberspace Operations Strategist to shape and drive AWS engagement across the Department of War (DoW) and wider U.S. Government (USG) cyberspace operations ecosystem. You will work at the intersection of cyberspace operations, policy, requirements, and capability development, engaging across the stakeholders and commands that shape and execute the DoW cyber mission — including the Office of the National Cyber Director (ONCD), the DoW Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Deputy CIO for Cybersecurity, U.S. Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM), the Department of Defense Cyber Defense Command (DCDC), the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), the Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and the Service Cyber Components. Internally, you will partner with the AWS Public Policy team, AWS Security, and other AWS teams to align AWS engagement and support into the DoW.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance.

Key job responsibilities
• Advise DoW leaders on how AWS supports their mission objectives across capability development, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and Zero Trust
• Partner with the AWS Public Policy team, AWS Security, and other AWS teams to align AWS engagement and support into the DoW
• Coordinate AWS engagement across the policy, oversight, resourcing, and operational stakeholders that shape and execute the DoW cyber mission
• Inform mission requirements and connect AWS solutions to the intelligence, operations, plans and policy, communications, and resource-integration functions of the DoW cyber mission
• Author strategy documents, decision papers, and executive briefings that support crisis response and critical-infrastructure resilience priorities

A day in the life
You will translate DoW and U.S. Government cyber priorities into AWS's engagement strategy, advising DoW leaders on how AWS supports their mission objectives. The role demands fluency across the full span of the cyber mission — from Zero Trust architecture, identity, credential, and access management (ICAM), and threat intelligence sharing partnerships to the offensive, defensive, and hunt-forward operations executed by the Cyber Mission Force (CMF) and its threat-aligned task forces and program offices. It also requires fluency in cyber policy, enabling you to engage effectively with public policy advocates, interagency partners, and national cyber leadership.

About the team
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or above
- Experience developing strategies that influence leadership decisions at the organizational level
- 7+ years of professional or military experience in cyber strategy, policy, or operations within or alongside the Department of War (DoW), the Intelligence Community, or the interagency cyber enterprise
- Experience in verbal and written communication for executive-level leaders, including briefing senior military and civilian leadership
- Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret or above

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, or a related field
- Knowledge of the DoW cyberspace enterprise, including United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM), the Cyber Mission Force construct - Cyber National Mission Teams, Cyber Combat Mission Teams, and Cyber Protection Teams, and the Service Cyber Components
